1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Avinash Pandey, learned Counsel for the complainant and perused the record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.20 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376,
504, 506 IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Dilippur, District Pratapgarh.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the applicant had enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years on 31.01.2024.

Subsequently after the recovery of the victim after about 5 days, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 05.02.2024 Farooq Ali Alias Sheboo vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...

wherein she stated that she was in love with the applicant for the last three years and they used to talk together.

She also stated that she had gone along with the applicant on 01.02.2024 and they stayed together in a room and physical relations were also formed and on 05.02.2024 her father recovered her from the place where they stayed, however, in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim gave a statement, which was at variance and stated that on 31.01.2024, the applicant had caught hold her and took her to a room and there she was kept for six days and wrong was also done on her.
It was also stated that the applicant was the son to her grandfather and was her uncle.
It was also stated that he used to come her home.

4. In the light of the said allegations, the Counsel for the applicant argues that admittedly in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim had admitted that she was love with the applicant and was gone with him.
He further argues that the tentative age of the victim is around 16 years.

My attention is also drawn to the statement of the victim recorded during trial, wherein, she stated that when she had come to her home, the mother and father made her understand for 3-4 days and thereafter she went with her parents and get the statement recorded.
She also stated that she had given the statement as directed by her parents.
She also stated that she did not know the applicant.
In the cross-examination where a question was put with the victim with regard to the property dispute in between the parties, she admitted that there was a dispute in between the parties.
The medical on record does not corroborate any allegations of any forceful sexual relation.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the huge variance in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and the cross-examination coupled with the fact that even in terms of the FIR, the name of the applicant was taken in the cross-examination; the victim had even denied knowing her and also considering the fact that there is a dispute in between the parties with regard to some property; the age of the victim is around 17 years; the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 06.02.2024 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Farooq Ali alias Sheboo be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Farooq Ali Alias Sheboo vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
